entries.question: Who was Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel?

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Jean-Paul Sartre?
entries.text: Jean-Paul Charles Aymard Sartre (21 June 1905 – 15 April 1980) was a French existentialist philosopher, novelist, playwright, screenwriter, and critic. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature for 1964, but refused it, saying "a writer should not allow himself to be turned into an institution".

entries.text: Jesus (or Jesus Christ, or Jesus of Nazareth) was a Jewish preacher and reformer of religion and the central figure of Christianity. In Christian tradition, Jesus is believed to be the Jewish Messiah mentioned in the Hebrew Bible.
entries.title: Jesus

entries.question: What is Ashoka?
entries.text: Ashoka was the greatest emperor of the Mauryan Empire. He ruled from 268–232 BC.
entries.title: Ashoka

entries.title: Charles de Gaulle

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Abraham Lincoln?
entries.text: Abraham Lincoln ( LINK-ən; February 12, 1809 – April 15, 1865) was an American politician who served as the 16th president of the United States from 1861 until his assassination in 1865.
entries.title: Abraham Lincoln

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Mao Zedong (26 December 1893 – 9 September 1976) was a Chinese Communist politician and revolutionary. He was also called Chairman Mao, because he was the first Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) from 1943 until his death in 1976.

entries.text: Nikola Tesla (Smiljan, July 10, 1856 - New York, January 7, 1943) was an American inventor and engineer of Serbian origin. He is best known for his contributions to the design of the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
